seo.title: Google Business Profile Service Area: Setup Guide
seo.meta_description: How to set a Google Business Profile service area in Anaheim and Orange County: service-area versus hybrid businesses, the 20-area limit and Google's rules.

h1: Google Business Profile Service Area: How to Set It Up the Right Way
answer: A Google Business Profile service area shows where you serve customers when they do not come to you. Service-area businesses hide their address and list up to 20 cities, postal codes or areas; hybrid businesses show their storefront and add a service area. Google says areas cannot be a radius and should stay within about 2 hours of driving from your base, which suits most Anaheim and Orange County trades.
key_takeaways: Hybrid businesses show a storefront and a service area.
You can list up to 20 service areas.
Radius service areas are no longer supported.
Keep it within about 2 hours of driving.

sections.heading: What a service area is
sections.body_html: Google's help page says your service area shows customers where you provide your products and services and helps people find your Business Profile. It is the setting that lets a plumber in Anaheim, a cleaner in Irvine or a mobile mechanic anywhere in Orange County appear for customers in the cities they cover, without showing a home address.

sections.heading: Service-area or hybrid business?
sections.body_html: Google defines a service-area business as one that visits or delivers to customers but does not serve them at its business address, with cleaning services and plumbers as examples. A hybrid business serves customers at its address and also visits or delivers to them, such as a dine-in restaurant that delivers. Hybrid businesses can show their storefront address, set hours for when staff are available and add a service area.

sections.heading: Remove your address if customers don't visit
sections.body_html: Google is direct: if you do not serve customers at your business address, remove the address from your profile. It also says a business without permanent on-site signage is not eligible as a storefront and should be listed as a service-area business. Service-area businesses can only have one profile for the whole area they serve.

sections.heading: Who must have a storefront
sections.body_html: Google notes that businesses with products or services that have an age requirement, such as alcohol, cannabis or weapons, need to have a storefront. They cannot be set up as service-area-only profiles.

sections.heading: How to add or edit a service area
sections.body_html: Go to your Business Profile, select Edit profile, then Location, and next to Service area select Edit. Choose a suggested area or type one in, then save. Google says you can set up to 20 service areas based on cities, postal codes or other areas, and that approved edits may take up to 48 hours to show.

sections.heading: No more radius areas
sections.body_html: Google's help page says you cannot set a service area as a radius around your business. If you set one up that way in the past, you cannot edit it; you must specify your area by city, postal code or another type of area instead. Many older Orange County profiles still have a radius and need updating.

sections.heading: How far is too far
sections.body_html: Google advises that the boundaries of your overall area should not be more than about 2 hours of driving time from where your business is based, and to be as specific and accurate as possible. List the places you genuinely serve, not every city in Southern California.

sections.heading: Choosing your 20 areas in Orange County
sections.body_html: Orange County had 3,186,989 residents in the 2020 census, spread across many cities. With 20 slots, start with the cities where your customers actually are and where you can respond quickly, such as Anaheim, Fullerton, Orange, Garden Grove and Santa Ana for a north-county business, then add postal codes or nearby cities that bring real jobs.

sections.heading: Service areas and rankings
sections.body_html: Google says local results are mainly based on relevance, distance and popularity. A service area tells Google where you work, but distance from your verified location still plays a part, so a business based in Anaheim will not rank equally everywhere it lists. Back the areas up with real projects and reviews from those cities.

sections.heading: Service area pages on your website
sections.body_html: Add a service area page that lists the cities you cover and links to project examples from each. Avoid dozens of near-identical city pages, which Google's spam policies treat as doorway abuse.

sections.heading: Service area checklist
sections.body_html:
• Business type is set correctly: service-area or hybrid.
  • Address removed if customers do not visit it.
  • No more than 20 service areas.
  • Areas are cities, postal codes or regions, not a radius.
  • The whole area is within about 2 hours of driving.
  • Every listed area is somewhere you genuinely work.
  • Website service area page lists the same places.
  • Real projects or reviews from those places are shown.

sections.heading: An example
sections.body_html: Imagine a plumber who works from home in Anaheim and drives to customers. The profile hides the home address and lists cities the business genuinely covers, such as Anaheim, Fullerton, Orange, Placentia, Yorba Linda, Garden Grove and Santa Ana, rather than every city in the county. The website has one service area page naming those cities, with a few real jobs from each. If the plumber later rents a showroom where customers can visit during set hours with permanent signage, the profile can become a hybrid business showing that address alongside the service area.

sections.heading: How this fits your local plan
sections.body_html: Treat this as part of a routine rather than a one-off fix. Local visibility in Anaheim and the rest of Orange County comes from many small, accurate signals adding up: a verified profile, consistent listings, useful service pages, real photos and a flow of honest reviews. Google is open that relevance, distance and popularity drive local results. You cannot change distance, but you can make sure Google and AI assistants understand exactly what you do and see evidence that customers value it. Put a monthly reminder in the calendar to check the profile, read new reviews and update anything that has changed.

sections.heading: What to do this week
sections.body_html:
1. Decide: service-area or hybrid.
  2. Remove the address if customers do not visit.
  3. Replace any radius with cities or postal codes.
  4. Update the service area page on your site.

sections.heading: When to get help
sections.body_html: Most of this can be done in-house with an hour or two and careful reading of Google's own help pages. It is worth bringing in help when the stakes are high or the problem keeps coming back: a profile that has been suspended more than once, many locations to manage, a site that keeps failing the same checks, or no time to keep up the routine. A good local SEO partner should explain what they will change and why, point to Google's guidelines rather than promise rankings, and leave you with access to every account. Chimera works this way with businesses across Anaheim and Orange County.

sections.heading: The short version
sections.body_html: Pick the right business type, hide your address if customers do not visit, list up to 20 real areas within about 2 hours of driving and replace any old radius. Chimera, based in Anaheim, sets up service areas for trades across Orange County.

faqs.q: How many service areas can I add on Google?
faqs.a: Up to 20, based on cities, postal codes or other areas.

faqs.q: Can I set my service area as a radius?
faqs.a: No. Google no longer supports radius service areas.

faqs.q: Should I hide my address on Google Business Profile?
faqs.a: Yes, if you do not serve customers at your business address.

faqs.q: How far can my service area reach?
faqs.a: Google says the overall area should not be more than about 2 hours of driving from your base.

faqs.q: How long do service area changes take?
faqs.a: Google says approved edits may take up to 48 hours to show.

faqs.q: Can a service-area business have several profiles?
faqs.a: No. Google says service-area businesses can only have one profile for the whole area they serve.
